summary: Intermittent inference stalls during hourly token-burst followed by client retry waves
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports periodic 'timeout' and long tail responses for streaming and non-streaming generation during their hourly batch jobs. Impact: Multiple user-facing features in MediSync slowed (patient summary generation), causing degraded UX for ~5-10% of requests during incident windows. Pattern: spikes align to top-of-hour batch fanout (customer-side) and correlate with a short window of 429s returned by our endpoints. Customer perceives model hang/timeouts rather than throttling because retries appear to be queuing and not immediate errors.

High level timeline:
- 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC: first report received from customer support engineer.
- 2026-03-11 09:10 UTC: initial support troubleshooting; observed elevated p95/p99 latency for /v1/generate.
- 2026-03-11 10:05 UTC: SRE reproduced pattern in prod via load replay.
- 2026-03-12 02:30 UTC: temporary mitigation applied (increase soft burst for customer).

Why this is confusing to customers: our soft quota policy returns 429 as an admission signal which many SDKs/clients automatically retry with short fixed backoffs. The combination of a burst of requests from the customer and immediate client retries amplifies traffic into a retry wave that pushes requests into our queueing window; instead of immediate 429s, requests get enqueued and experience long tail latency, which looks like a model slowdown or timeout to the client.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From a client machine, simulate a 300-concurrent request fanout against the hosted endpoint (POST /v1/generate) using same payload size as MediSync (avg 800 tokens expected).
2) Configure SDK to use default retry behavior (no jitter, initial backoff 100ms, max retries 6).
3) Fire batch at top-of-hour and observe status codes and response latencies.
4) Compare behavior when toggling client backoff to exponential+full jitter (initial 200ms).

Minimal repro curl snippet (single request to reproduce 429 window):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"<~800 token prompt>","max_tokens":512}'

Load replay notes: we used k6 to replay customer traffic with and without retry amplification and saw p99 jump from ~1200ms to >12s during amplified retry waves.

observed: several client IPs repeatedly sending identical requests 6-10x within 1-2s windows (retry amplification).
Edge metrics snapshot (09:02-09:06 UTC): 429 count +820, queued_requests +310, p99 latency spike to 12.8s.
Correlated with customer logs: their SDK reports 'stream timed out after 10s' while our backend eventually returns 200 after queuing.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: model serving regression.
What we checked: model runtime CPU/GPU utilization, kernel errors, serving node OOMs — all normal for window. No model-level regressions in 09:00 window.
Observed: quota enforcement produced short 429s which were sometimes followed by the request being retried and enqueued instead of rejected. The enqueueing came from internal ingress queueing when capacity headroom was low (reserved pool for dedicated customers was close to saturation).
Root cause drivers: 1) customer sends periodic burst (design): many small-ish requests at once. 2) client SDK default retry settings (fixed short backoff, aggressive retry count) cause retry amplification when 429s occur. 3) our soft quota/burst enforcement currently uses a short Retry-After and allows transient enqueueing that increases service queue length which then increases latency for queued requests. 4) autoscaler did not scale fast enough during the sub-minute spike because the spike duration fell within our stabilization window and we are at near-commit capacity for this dedicated pool.
Evidence: replay experiments show that replacing client retry behavior with exponential backoff+full jitter prevents the long tail even under identical RPS. Increasing soft-burst threshold for the customer removed the enqueueing but we treat this as temporary because it affects multi-tenant fairness.
Actions taken during investigation:
- Tuned customer's soft-burst quota up by +30% for 2 hours (mitigation).
- Collected and attached k6 load test artifacts and flamegraphs to internal PR.
- Opened INT-4521 to track autoscaler tuning for short spike responsiveness.
comments: Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-11T09:12:00Z: Customer reports that their UI shows 'generation timed out' during hourly sync. Asked for request ids and sample payloads. Provided initial logs and asked them to confirm concurrency and SDK version.

Customer (MediSync - Jake Lin) - 2026-03-11T09:20:00Z: Provided sample request ids rp_9a3f4, rp_9a6b2 and confirmed they use redwood-js-sdk v0.8.2 with default retry settings and a top-of-hour fanout job that hits 300 concurrent requests.

SRE (Miguel Hernandez) - 2026-03-11T10:12:00Z: Reproduced behavior in prod using k6 replay. Observed enqueueing and long-tail latency when SDK resubmits immediately after 429s. Not a model regression. Filed INT-4521 to look at scaler stabilization policy.

Support Engineering (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-12T02:35:00Z: Temporary mitigation applied: scaled up soft burst for MediSync for 2 hours. Customer confirmed immediate improvement. Recommended client retries be changed to exponential backoff with jitter. Documented SDK configuration guidance in ticket.
Customer (Jake Lin) - 2026-03-12T03:02:00Z: Confirmed improved behavior after temporary increase; asked for long-term fixes so they don't need to rely on quota increases.

SRE (Miguel Hernandez) - 2026-03-13T11:45:00Z: Follow-up: proposed changes: (1) default SDK retry policy update (exponential backoff + full jitter) in redwood-js-sdk v0.9.0, (2) add server-side per-customer circuit-breaker to fail fast after N 429s in 10s window, (3) adjust autoscaler short-window reaction thresholds for dedicated pools. PRs and runbook updates linked below.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: temporary soft-burst increase for MediSync (2 hours) which reduced enqueueing and p99 latency during incident windows. Longer-term plan: 1) SDK default change to exponential backoff + jitter (tracked in github PR), 2) implement server-side fast-fail circuit breaker for repeated 429s to avoid queue amplification, 3) adjust dedicated autoscaler to be more responsive to <30s spikes (INT-4521), 4) provide customer guidance and an example recommended configuration for scheduled batch jobs (stagger fanout, add client-side jitter).

Follow-ups assigned: Miguel Hernandez (INT-4521) to work autoscaler changes, Priya Nair to coordinate SDK default change (PR referenced), Support to send customer guidance doc and recommended client settings.

Post-incident notes: Added alerting for queue depth increases paired with rising 429 counts for dedicated customers to detect this pattern earlier.
